content.title: About
content.content: All‑purpose wheat flour is a versatile product milled from selected wheat varieties. It is neither enriched with vitamins and minerals nor bleached, preserving its natural yellowish hue and characteristic flavor. Suitable for bread, cakes, cookies, and most other culinary recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: All‑purpose flour combines the properties of bread and pastry flour, making it usable in a wide range of recipes.
Because it is unenriched, it retains the natural B‑vitamin content, though at lower levels than fortified flours.
Unbleached flour has a richer aroma and a slightly nutty taste compared to bleached varieties.
Wheat flour has been a staple in human diets for over 10,000 years.
In the US, product code 5643 often refers to standard all‑purpose wheat flour without additives.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides slow‑release energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: About 10 g of protein per 100 g, supporting tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Although not whole‑grain, it still offers a modest amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin, and folate support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Large portions can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to wheat.

items.title: Mycotoxin risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth that produces toxins.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Use the flour for baking bread, rolls, cakes, cookies, pancakes, and pizza dough. It can be partially substituted with whole‑grain flour to boost nutrition. Sifting before mixing helps eliminate lumps and aerates the flour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat rancidity.
